Stony
stō´ny
adj. (of stone, hard as stone; of ground, shallow over rock; rendering Hebrew eben, Greek petrodes)
Stone + y. Ezekiel's phrase is literally the heart of stone; the parable's is the rocky place, ground with rock a finger's depth beneath it.

Biblical Definition

God's promise of a new heart is stated as surgery: “A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh” (Eze 36:26; Eze 11:19). In the parable some seed “fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth” (Mat 13:5), and the Lord explains: “he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it; yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while” (Mat 13:20; Mar 4:16). David: “When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words; for they are sweet” (Psa 141:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines stony as made of stone; abounding with stones; hard, unfeeling, obdurate, as a stony heart.

expand to see more

STONY, a. Made of stone; as a stony tower.

2. Consisting of stone; abounding with stone; as stony ground.

3. Hard; unfeeling; obdurate; pitiless; as a stony heart.

Key Scripture

Eze 36:26 — "A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh."

Eze 11:19 — "And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh:"

Mat 13:5 — "Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth:"

Mat 13:20 — "But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;"

Mar 4:16 — "And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;"

Psa 141:6 — "When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words; for they are sweet."

Modern Corruption

Sinners are told to open their hearts, and Ezekiel says the heart is stone and God removes it.

expand to see more

The invitation to “open your heart to Jesus” assumes a heart with a hinge. Ezekiel describes a heart of stone, and a stone does not open; it is taken out. Every verb in Ezekiel 36:26 has God for its subject — I will give, I will put, I will take away, I will give — and the sinner is the patient on the table, not the surgeon. This is the doctrine of regeneration, and it is why the Reformed insist that the new birth precedes faith rather than following it: a stony heart cannot believe any more than it can beat. The man who did believe should look at the verse and understand what was done to him while he was under.

The stony-ground hearer is the parable's warning against counting joy as conversion. He hears the word and “anon with joy receiveth it” — the response every evangelist hopes for — and he has no root, and when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended. The seed sprang up fastest where the rock was nearest the surface, because the warmth had nowhere to go. A profession that comes quickly and gladly is not thereby false, but it is not thereby true either, and the decisionism that reports every stony-ground response as a harvest has confused the sprouting with the crop. The parable's test is not how the seed came up but whether it is still there when the sun is hot.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew eben (H68), a stone; Greek petrodes (G4075), rock-like, rocky; Hebrew sela (H5553), a crag.

expand to see more

Hebrew leb ha'eben (H3820, H68) — the heart of stone; Ezekiel 11:19, 36:26.

Greek petrodes (G4075) — rocky, stony; Matthew 13:5, 13:20, Mark 4:5, 4:16.

Hebrew sela (H5553) — a cliff, crag; Psalm 141:6, “stony places.”

Usage

"“I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh” — surgery, not an invitation."

"“Received the seed into stony places… anon with joy” — the sprout that is not a crop."

"“Where they had not much earth” — the rock a finger's depth down."
